_comment: Example profile showing every option. Copy to ~/.config/asbx/profiles/ and edit - real hosts and secret paths belong there, not in version control. `asbx profile show NAME` prints what a profile resolves to.
_comment_env: Non-secret values delivered to the guest as environment variables, alongside the capability placeholders. Base URLs and usernames go here; credentials never do.
_comment_aws_autosign: Opts the session into re-signing every AWS request the guest makes, for any AWS host the session's destination policy already allows - not one declared here. box start mints a random dummy AWS key for the guest (it never holds a real one); signing_secret is the real credential the broker signs with. aws_profile:NAME resolves live off ~/.aws, the same way `aws --profile NAME` would - no separate export step. file:/path also works, for a credential bundle kept fresh some other way (a CI secrets manager, say). See README's 'AWS requests' section.
_comment_browser_impersonation: Requests to these hosts leave the gateway with a real browser's TLS and HTTP/2 fingerprint (and its User-Agent, so the two agree) instead of mitmproxy's own - for sites behind bot protection, such as Cloudflare's, that refuse anything that doesn't look like a browser. Not a grant: the hosts still have to pass the session's policy. target is a curl_cffi name - chrome, safari, firefox, or a pinned version like chrome136.
_comment_injection: injection is always a list of rules. One entry, as in these three capabilities, is the ordinary case: one mechanism, unconditionally, and that rule's own 'when' is the capability's grant - there is no separate top-level 'when'. More than one rule dispatches by which one's 'when' a request actually matches, for a secret that needs different mechanisms at different destinations (see 'deploy tooling' below for a rule's other fields, and the README for a worked multi-rule example).

capabilities._comment_deny: deny_paths is checked before paths, so a broad allow can keep a few endpoints out of reach. Use it where an API mixes routine and destructive operations under one prefix. Capability-wide - not inside 'when' or any one injection rule - since it isn't about which mechanism attaches, it's about what the capability may touch at all.
capabilities._comment_ttl: ttl is in seconds, and 0 - the default - means the capability never expires, because an agent may run for days. Set it only for a grant meant to lapse on its own; extend one with `asbx cap renew`.
